source_text: Sed quomodo funditus euertetur antichristus, nisi ceteris quoque iniectionibus eius elidendis locus detur. relaxata praescriptionum defensione? accedamus igitur iam hinc ad ipsam dei personam, uel potius umbram et phantasma secundum Christum ipsius. per idque examinetur, per quod creatori praefertur. et utique erunt regulae certae ad examinandam dei bonitatem. sed prius est, ut inueniam illam et adprehendam. et ita ad regulas perducam. cum enim circumspicio tempora, nusquam est a primordio materiarum et introitu causarum. cum quibus debuerat inueniri, exinde agens, quo agere habuit. erat enim iam et mors et aculeus mortis, delictum, et ipsa malitia creatoris. aduersus quam subuenire deberet alterius dei bonitas, t primae huic regulae diuinae bonitatis occurrens, si se naturalem probaret, statim succurrens, ut causa coepit. omnia enim in deo naturalia et ingenita esse debebunt, ut sint aeterna, secundum statum ipsius, ne obuenticia et extranea reputentur ac per hoc temporalia et aeternitatis aliena. ita et bonitas perennis et iugis exigetur in deo, quae in thesauris naturalium proprietatum reposita et parata antecederet causas et materias suas, et primam quamque susciperet, non despiceret et destitueret, si antecedebat. denique non minus et hic quaeram, cur non a primordio operata sit bonitas eius, quam de ipso quaesiuimus, cur non a primordio sit reuelatus? quidni? qui per bonitatem reuelari haberet, si qui fuisset. non posse quid deo non licet, nedum naturalibus suis fungi. quae si continentur, quo minus currant, naturalia non erunt. et otium enim sui natura non nouit; hinc censetur, si agat. sic nec noluisse uidebitur exercere bonitatem, interim naturae nomine. natura enim se non potest nolle, quae se ita dirigit, ut, si cessauerit, non sit. sed cessauit aliquando in deo Marcionis de opere bonitas: ergo non fuit naturalis bonitas, quae potuit aliquando cessasse, quod naturalibus non licet. et si non erit naturalis, iam nec aeterna credenda nec deo par. quia non aeterna, dum non naturalis, quae denique nullam sui perpetuitatem aut de praeterito constituat aut de futuro repromittat. nam ut a primordio non fuit, et in finem sine dubio non erit. potest enim et non esse quandoque, sicut non fuit aliquando. igitur cum constet in primordio cessasse bonitatem dei illius — (non) enim a primordio liberauit hominem — et uoluntate potius eam quam infirmitate cessasse, iam uoluntas subpressae bonitatis finis inuenietur malignitatis. quid enim tam malignum quam nolle prodesse cum possis,, quam utilitatem cruciare, quam iniuriam sinere? totum denique creatoris elogium in illum rescribetur, qui saeuitias eius i bonitatis suae mora iuuit. nam in cuius manu est quid ne fiat, eius iam deputatur, cum fit. homo damnatur in mortem ob unius arbusculae delibationem, et exinde proficiunt delicta cum poenis et pereunt iam omnes, qui paradisi nullum caespitem norunt. et hoc melior aliqui deus aut nescit aut sustinet? si ut ex hoc melior inueniretur, quanto creator deterior haberetur. satis et in isto consilio malitiosus, qui et illum uoluit oneratum, operationibus eius admissis, et saeculum in uexatione detinuit. quid de tali medico iudicabis, qui nutriat morbum mora praesidii et periculum extendat dilatione remedii, quo pretiosius aut famosius curet? talis et in deum Marcionis dicenda sententia est, mali permissorem, iniuriae fautorem, gratiae lenocinatorem, benignitatis praeuaricatorem, quam non statim causae suae exhibuit; plane exhibiturus, si natura bonus et non accessione, si ingenio optimus et non disciplina, si ab aeuo deus et non a Tiberio, immo, quod uerius, a Cerdone et Marcione. Tiberio nunc deus ille praestiterit, ut imperio eius diuina bonitas in terris dedicaretur,
pass_a_gloss: But how will the antichrist be completely overthrown, unless also the other injections of his are to be destroyed, with the defense of prescriptions being relaxed? Let us approach, therefore, from here the very person of God, or rather the shadow and phantom according to Christ himself. And let it be examined through that by which it is preferred to the creator. And certainly there will be certain rules for examining the goodness of God. But first, it is necessary that I find and grasp it, and thus lead it to the rules. For when I look around at the times, it is nowhere from the beginning of things and the introduction of causes. With which it ought to have been found, from then on acting, since it had the power to act. For already death and the sting of death, sin, and the malice itself of the creator existed. Against which the goodness of another God ought to have come to aid, as the first rule of divine goodness, if it proved itself to be natural, immediately assisting, as soon as the cause began. For all things in God ought to be natural and innate, so that they may be eternal, according to his state, lest they be considered adventitious and foreign, and thus temporal and alien to eternity. So also the goodness ought to be perpetual and constant in God, which, deposited and prepared in the treasures of natural properties, would precede its causes and materials, and would undertake the first of all, not despising or abandoning them, if it preceded them. Finally, I will also ask here, why his goodness did not operate from the beginning, just as we asked why he himself was not revealed from the beginning. Why not? For he who was to be revealed through goodness, if he existed. It is not possible for God not to be able to do something, especially to function with his natural properties. If these are restrained, why do they not run, if they are not natural? For even inactivity is not known to his nature; hence, it is considered, if he acts. So also it will not seem that he was unwilling to exercise his goodness, meanwhile, in the name of nature. For nature cannot be unwilling, which directs itself in such a way that, if it ceases, it is not. But the goodness of God, according to Marcion, ceased from his work at some time; therefore, it was not natural goodness, which was able to cease at some time, which is not permitted to natural things. And if it is not natural, it is not to be believed to be eternal, nor equal to God. Because it is not eternal, since it is not natural, which finally constitutes no perpetuity of itself, either from the past or promised for the future. For just as it was not from the beginning, so it will certainly not be in the end. For it is possible for it also not to exist at some time, just as it did not exist at some time. Therefore, since it is established that the goodness of that God ceased at the beginning - for it did not free man from the beginning - and that it ceased by will rather than weakness, the end of the suppressed goodness will be found to be malice. For what is as malicious as not to wish to benefit when one can, as to torture utility, as to permit injury? Finally, the whole eulogy of the creator will be rewritten against him, who helped his cruelties with the delay of his goodness. For in whose hand it is that something is not done, it is already imputed to him, when it is done. Man is condemned to death for the eating of one little tree, and from then on sins proceed with punishments, and all who know no grass of paradise already perish. And does some better God either not know or tolerate this? If, so that he might be found better from this, how much worse the creator would be considered. It is enough that he is malicious even in this counsel, who willed that he be burdened with his operations, and detained the age in vexation. What will you judge of such a doctor, who nourishes the disease by delaying aid and extends the danger by delaying the remedy, so that he may treat it more precious or famous? Such a sentence is to be spoken also against the God of Marcion, the permitter of evil, the favorer of injury, the pimp of grace, the transgressor of benignity, who did not immediately exhibit his cause; he would have exhibited it, if he were good by nature and not by acquisition, if he were optimal by genius and not by discipline, if he were God from eternity and not from Tiberius, or rather, what is truer, from Cerdo and Marcion. Now that God will have surpassed Tiberius, so that the divine goodness might be dedicated on earth by his empire.

pass_b_english: How can the Antichrist be utterly overthrown unless room is also given to dismantle his other injections, now that the defense of prescriptions has been relaxed? Let us therefore move from here to the very person of God—or rather, to the shadow and phantom according to Christ himself—and examine him through that by which he is preferred to the Creator. There will certainly be fixed rules for testing the goodness of God, but first I must find and grasp it, and so bring it before those rules. When I survey the times, it is nowhere to be found from the beginning of matter and the entrance of causes; it ought to have been found with them, acting from then on, since it had the power to act. For already death and the sting of death, sin, and the very malice of the Creator existed. Against these the goodness of another God ought to have come to aid, as the first rule of divine goodness: if it proved itself natural, it would have assisted immediately, as soon as the cause began. For everything in God ought to be natural and innate, so that it may be eternal, according to his state, lest it be considered adventitious and foreign, and thus temporal and alien to eternity. So also perpetual and constant goodness ought to exist in God—deposited and prepared in the treasures of natural properties—so that it would precede its causes and materials, and would undertake the very first one, not despising or abandoning it, if it indeed preceded them. Finally I must also ask here why his goodness did not operate from the beginning, just as we asked why he himself was not revealed from the beginning. Why not? He who was to be revealed through goodness, if he existed. It is not possible for God to be unable to do something, let alone to function with his natural properties. If these are restrained, why do they not run? They would not be natural. For even inactivity is not known to his nature; hence it is recognized only when it acts. So it will not appear that he was unwilling to exercise his goodness, meanwhile, in the name of nature. For nature cannot be unwilling—it directs itself so that if it ceases, it is not. But the goodness of Marcion's God ceased from his work at some time; therefore it was not natural goodness, which was able to cease at some time—something not permitted to natural things. And if it is not natural, it is not to be believed eternal, nor equal to God. Because it is not eternal, since it is not natural, it finally constitutes no perpetuity of itself, either from the past or promised for the future. For just as it was not from the beginning, so it certainly will not be in the end. For it is possible for it also not to exist at some time, just as it did not exist at some time. And does some better God either not know or tolerate this? If he might be found better from this, how much worse the Creator would be considered. He is malicious enough even in this counsel, who willed that he be burdened with his operations, and detained the age in vexation. What will you judge of such a doctor, who nourishes the disease by delaying aid and extends the danger by delaying the remedy, so that he may treat it more precious or famous? Such a sentence is to be spoken also against the God of Marcion, the permitter of evil, the favorer of injury, the pimp of grace, the transgressor of benignity, who did not immediately exhibit his cause; he would have exhibited it, if he were good by nature and not by acquisition, if he were optimal by genius and not by discipline, if he were God from eternity and not from Tiberius—or rather, what is truer, from Cerdo and Marcion.
